newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX backs rise in energy contract position limit.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX backs rise in energy contract position limit.

text.p: New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) said Thursday it has approved expanded position limits for its four largest energy futures contracts: crude oil, natural gas, heating oil and gasoline.

The maximum number of crude oil futures that may be held overnight will be expanded to 15,000 contracts from 10,000 contracts, the limit for Henry Hub natural gas futures will rise to 12,000 contracts from 7,000, and the limit on heating and gasoline futures will be increased to 10,000 contracts from 7,000.
The single month limit for crude oil, natural gas and heating oil will be expanded to 7,500 contracts from 5,000 while the single month limit for gasoline will remain at 5,000 contracts.
The expiration position limits for all the energy contracts, in effect for the last three days of trading, will remain at 1,000 contracts.
NYMEX said the increase in position limits must be approved by Commodity Futures Trading Commission before they can be implemented.
